Chapter 11: Living with Childlike Wonder
Have you ever noticed how, as we grow up, we tend to lose that wide-eyed sense of wonder we had as kids? The world gets familiar, routines take over, and before you know it, curiosity just slips away. But here’s something beautiful—love actually needs wonder to grow. It thrives when we’re willing to see the world, and each other, through fresh eyes.
Let me share a story. There was a grandfather who took his granddaughter for a walk in the woods. She stopped at every little thing—every leaf, every bug, every sunbeam peeking through the trees. And as he slowed down to share that wonder with her, he started to notice things he hadn’t seen in years. By the time they finished their walk, he felt lighter, more alive. It was a real eye-opener—wonder isn’t just for kids. It’s really about being present, about finding beauty in the everyday things we usually overlook.
Most of us get caught up in the rush of daily life, only focusing on what needs to get done. But love? It asks us to pause. To pay attention. To find delight in the small stuff.
One friend told me how she started a gratitude journal, jotting down three things each day that surprised or delighted her. Over time, she noticed her whole outlook shifting—she became more patient, more joyful, and even more open to the people around her.
Living with wonder means letting go of cynicism, that feeling that you’ve seen it all before. It’s about being open to surprise, to feeling moved, and maybe even changed. So many people don’t realize how much they’re missing when they stop really noticing the world around them. But here’s the thing—when you choose to pay attention, wonder opens your heart, and that’s where love truly begins to grow.
